article.title: Common mistake: 'from' vs 'since' for time
article.description: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'
article.content: Wrong: 'I have lived here from 2015.' Right: 'I have lived here since 2015.' Teaching point: use 'since' with present perfect for a starting point still relevant now; 'from' is used with a defined start AND end point, like 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.'

generated.caption:
Ever mixed up 'from' and 'since' when talking about time? 🤔 It's a common one!

Use **'since'** with the present perfect to mark a start point that's *still continuing*. For a period with a *clear start AND end*, you'll use **'from'**.

So, it's "I have lived here **since** 2015." Or, "The offer is valid **from** Monday to Friday."

Save this tip! Follow @TheEnglishVault for daily English boosters!
generated.script:
"I have lived here from 2015." Sunne mein theek lagta hai na? But isme ek chhoti si galti hai!

Dekho, jab hum present perfect tense mein batate hain ki koi cheez kab se start hui aur abhi tak chal rahi hai, tab hum **since** use karte hain. Jaise, 'I have lived here since 2015.' Matlab, 2015 se reh raha hoon aur abhi bhi yahi rehta hoon. Aur **from**? Woh tab use hota hai jab ek definite start aur end point dono ho. Jaise, 'The offer is valid from Monday to Friday.' Samjha?

Toh, next time, jo cheez abhi bhi chal rahi hai, uska starting point batane ke liye **since**! Aur jab ek start aur end dono clear ho, tab **from**! Ab samajh aaya?

slides.headlineRest: For Time Can Be Wrong — Here's Why
slides.body: Many English learners mistakenly use 'from' when referring to a starting point in the past that continues until now. For instance, saying "I have lived here from 2015" is incorrect. Instead, when talking about an action or state that began in the past and is still ongoing, always use 'since' with the present perfect tense: "I have lived here since 2015." The word 'from' is reserved for situations where both a start and an end point are clearly defined, such as "The offer is valid from Monday to Friday." Remember this distinction to sound more natural and accurate!
